plain: In 1947, after many UFO sightings across the United States, a senior Air Force general named Nathan Twining wrote a letter that is now known as the Twining memo. Podcast host Jesse Michels describes Twining as the head of all aircraft development for the Air Force and places the letter at Air Materiel Command, the branch that handled aircraft development and testing. Michels says Twining sent it to Brigadier General George Schulgen. In Michels's words, the memo said the objects were real, "neither visionary nor fictitious", meaning not imagined and not made up. He tells the story on several episodes and in one ties it to an observation program in Alaska. A guest named Merrick adds that Twining later became chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, the top military advisers to the president, and that the memo listed the features of the objects. The story's title also points to a closing note in the memo about separate, independent programs, though the tellings here do not spell it out. It matters to the tellers because, if true, it shows a top general treating UFOs as real from the very start.
